question: Does a standard compact parent of Pati-Salam put the complete selected Dirac and Majorana portal complexes in one involutive orbit with exactly one invariant contraction?

scope.orbitMeaning: an involution normalizing the chosen Pati-Salam stage and mapping the complete typed operator complex, including scalar, family character, grading and J data
scope.oneContractionMeaning: multiplicity one after both gauge representation and the actual family-labelled coefficient space are included
notSearched: arbitrary product groups without a natural Pati-Salam embedding

sources.use: explicit Spin(10)-to-Pati-Salam invariant decomposition and D parity
E6 matter 27 and scalar 351-prime decompositions and Yukawa sector
E6 351-prime parent relation between Spin(10) 10 and 126 Yukawa sectors and threshold boundary

patiSalamData.familyBoundary: The selected Dirac and selected-null Majorana coefficients occupy different entries in the marked family coefficient matrix and carry different low-energy family dressings.

involutionInvariant.normalizerRule: An involution descending to the chosen Pati-Salam stage permutes Pati-Salam irreducibles through a group automorphism and therefore preserves representation dimension and tensor invariants.
involutionInvariant.dimensionConsequence: No complete sourced Dirac scalar multiplet has the dimension of a sourced Majorana scalar multiplet, so none can be exchanged as whole Pati-Salam representations by a normalizer involution.
involutionInvariant.familyConsequence: Even a parent gauge tensor does not exchange a neutral selected Dirac family entry with the charge-minus-three selected-null entry unless the parent also contains the marked family symmetry and its intertwiner.

candidateAudit.matterResult: F_L and F_R can be parity partners
candidateAudit.scalarOrbit: H_D is mapped to a bidoublet of the same type; H_MR is mapped to the left Majorana partner H_ML, not to H_D

candidateAudit.matterResult: the Sp(4) fundamental branches as (2,1)+(1,2), so left and right weak matter types can share one parent representation
candidateAudit.weakScalarResult: the Sp(4) adjoint branches as (3,1)+(1,3)+(2,2), so weak triplet and bidoublet types can share one parent representation
candidateAudit.su4Obstruction: a product-group irrep has one fixed SU(4) representation across those weak branches, whereas H_D uses SU(4) 1 or 15 and H_M uses 10 or 6
candidateAudit.verdict: smallest clear near-miss; fails the SU(4) scalar type

candidateAudit.minimalDiracH1PlusMajorana: H_D1 in 10H and H_MR in 126H use two inequivalent parent invariant tensors and two Yukawa matrices
candidateAudit.shared126NearMiss: Choosing the sourced H_D15 branch and H_MR from one 126H puts both gauge components in the single multiplicity-one 16F 16F 126H invariant.
candidateAudit.involutionTest: D parity fixes/exchanges bidoublet chirality within its type and maps H_MR to H_ML. The D5 diagram automorphism conjugates spinor/self-dual representations; neither maps the bidoublet submultiplet to H_MR.
candidateAudit.actualSelectedCoefficientCount: at least two entries of the symmetric family Yukawa matrix Y_126
candidateAudit.verdict: smallest one-parent-tensor near-miss, but not an involutive orbit and not one selected numerical coefficient

candidateAudit.tensorProduct: 27 x 27 contains conjugate 27, 351 and 351-prime channels with multiplicity one; restriction to one 351-prime Yukawa channel gives one E6 invariant tensor
candidateAudit.oneTensorNearMiss: The 10H and 126H Spin(10) branches occur in one 351-prime, so one E6 Yukawa tensor fixes their relative Clebsch coefficients.
candidateAudit.outerAutomorphismTest: The E6 diagram involution sends 27 to bar(27) and 351-prime to its conjugate; it does not exchange the internal Spin(10) 10 and 126 branches. Any involution normalizing the selected Pati-Salam subgroup also preserves whole-multiplet dimensions.
candidateAudit.extraSpectrum: Each matter 27 adds a Spin(10) 10 plus singlet beyond the family 16; the 351-prime adds 1,16,54 and 144 scalar branches in addition to 10 and 126.
candidateAudit.actualSelectedCoefficientCount: at least two entries of the E6 family Yukawa matrix
candidateAudit.verdict: strongest single-tensor parent but no exchange involution and substantial extra spectrum

candidateAudit.matterResult: exchange maps each representation in copy A to the identical representation in copy B
candidateAudit.scalarOrbit: D_A maps to D_B and M_A maps to M_B; inequivalent D and M types remain separate orbits
candidateAudit.verdict: exact copy exchange reproduces the claim-1534 two-orbit mirror closure

familyMultiplicityAudit.oneParentTensorDoesNotMeanOneNumber: For n family copies, a symmetric parent Yukawa channel carries a symmetric n x n matrix, of dimension n(n+1)/2.
selectedEntries: Y_PP for the selected Dirac channel
Y_PN for the selected-null Majorana channel
familyMultiplicityAudit.independence: Gauge unification alone does not equate different family-matrix entries.
familyMultiplicityAudit.requiredRepair: a family symmetry/intertwiner that puts the two selected entries in one orbit while preserving the null mask

oneTensorVersusOrbit.oneTensor: Spin(10) with a shared 126H, or E6 with a 351-prime H, can derive fixed gauge Clebsches from one parent invariant tensor.
oneTensorVersusOrbit.oneOrbit: None of the audited normalizer involutions exchanges the complete D and M Pati-Salam multiplets.
oneTensorVersusOrbit.physicalMeaning: A one-tensor construction is a viable alternative mechanism to the claim-1528 exchange ansatz, but only after family-entry alignment, vacuum projection, threshold matching and unwanted-component control are proved.

ranking.reason: smallest parent with a multiplicity-one gauge tensor containing H_D15 and H_MR; fails involutive orbit and family-entry uniqueness
one tensor contains Spin(10) 10 and 126 branches and can relate their Yukawas; adds exotics and still fails orbit/family tests
smaller and unifies weak left-right types, but cannot unify the SU(4) scalar representations

ranking.candidate: left-right or doubled Pati-Salam semidirect products
ranking.reason: their involutions only exchange chirality or identical copies, leaving D and M in separate orbits

strongestConclusion: No audited standard compact parent realizes both requirements simultaneously: a complete involutive D/M portal orbit and one actual selected-family contraction. Spin(10) and E6 do furnish multiplicity-one gauge tensors containing both kinds of component, which is a distinct and more promising mechanism than exchange, but family multiplicity and symmetry-breaking data prevent promotion to the required common coefficient line.
reopeningDatum: For the leading Spin(10) route, specify one 126H Yukawa tensor using the (15,2,2) Dirac and (10,1,3) Majorana branches, then construct a family symmetry that relates the exact Y_PP and Y_PN entries, prove the selected vacuum/threshold projection preserves their fixed Clebsch ray, and audit all other 126 components. For a literal exchange, exhibit an enlarged parent and involution normalizing the low-energy embedding that maps the whole unequal-dimensional Pati-Salam multiplets, which requires structure beyond the audited ordinary group embeddings.
verdict: The literal involutive-orbit programme is negative for left-right parity, SU(4)xSp(4), Spin(10), E6 and doubled Pati-Salam. The highest-value surviving route is not exchange but a single parent invariant: shared-126 Spin(10) first, then E6 351-prime if the Dirac singlet and Majorana 126 channels must both be retained.
